prompt: A request matches a rule whose action is Count. What happens next?

choices.text: It is refused at once with a 403 Forbidden
choices.why: That is Block.

choices.text: Evaluation goes on to the next rule
choices.why: Right. Count records the match and passes the request on.

choices.text: It goes straight to the application
choices.why: That is Allow, which skips the later rules.

choices.text: The browser has to solve a puzzle first
choices.why: That is CAPTCHA.

prompt: An Allow rule for the office's addresses is placed at priority 0, above the managed rules. What does that do to a request from the office?

choices.text: It skips every rule below, managed rules included
choices.why: Right. And it leaves no trace of the rules it skipped.

choices.text: Nothing, since managed rules always run
choices.why: A terminating Allow stops evaluation; the managed rules never see it.

choices.text: It is checked twice, once per rule
choices.why: The first terminating match decides; there is no second check.

choices.text: It is blocked, since Allow rules are refused above managed groups
choices.why: WAF accepts the rule; the order is the team's decision.

prompt: What does a web ACL do with a request that no Block or Allow rule matched?
hint: It has an action of its own.

choices.text: Blocks it, as WAF denies by default
choices.why: The default action is configured, and public sites use Allow.

choices.text: Sends it to a CAPTCHA
choices.why: Only if a rule says so.

choices.text: Logs it and then drops the connection without a reply
choices.why: There is no such action.

choices.text: Applies the default action
choices.why: Right. For the shop that is Allow.

prompt: How many WCU does a web ACL's base request price include before each request costs more?
The first create-web-acl failed with 'Invalid base64: "/login"'. Which part of the system refused it?

choices.text: WAF, because /login is not a valid path
choices.why: The request never left the computer.

choices.text: moto, which does not support rate-based rules
choices.why: moto accepted the same file a moment later.

choices.text: The command line, reading a binary field from JSON
choices.why: Right. It expected base64 until told the file is plain text.

choices.text: The load balancer, before the association
choices.why: The web ACL did not exist yet.

prompt: To make the command line read binary fields of a JSON file as plain text, add --cli-binary-format ____. (one value)
moto reported the shop's web ACL at 3 capacity units. What would AWS report?
hint: The common rule set alone is 700.

choices.text: 3, the same as moto
choices.why: moto charges one unit a rule; AWS charges by the work.

choices.text: About 705
choices.why: Right. 700 for the common rule set, and a few for the IP set and the rate rule.

choices.text: 1,500, the included capacity
choices.why: That is the tier boundary, not this web ACL's size.

choices.text: 5,000, the maximum
choices.why: That is the ceiling a web ACL may reach.

prompt: Why does the shop override SizeRestrictions_BODY to Count instead of removing the common rule set?
hint: One rule misfires; the others are useful.

choices.text: Overrides are cheaper than removing a group
choices.why: The price is the same either way.

choices.text: A managed group cannot be removed once attached
choices.why: It can; it is one rule.

choices.text: Count makes the uploads faster
choices.why: Count changes the action, not the speed.

choices.text: Uploads exceed 8 KB; the other rules still block
choices.why: Right. Fix the false positive, keep the protection.

prompt: An address over the login-rate limit slows down below it. What happens to its requests?

choices.text: Let through again, on their own
choices.why: Right. The rule blocks only while the rate is over the limit.

choices.text: They stay blocked until someone removes the block
choices.why: A rate-based rule lifts its own block.

choices.text: The address is moved to the IP set
choices.why: WAF does not edit IP sets.

choices.text: They are sent to a CAPTCHA for a day
choices.why: The rule's action is Block, with no memory beyond the window.

prompt: A program tries passwords at 4 requests a second against /login, with a limit of 100 in 300 seconds. After how many seconds has it sent the 100th request?
Behind a mobile carrier, 40 customers share one address and the app retries a failed login 5 times. What does a limit of 100 per 5 minutes risk?

choices.text: Letting the attacker through
choices.why: That risk is a thousand addresses each under the limit, a separate case.

choices.text: Raising the WAF bill sharply
choices.why: Requests are priced the same whether blocked or not.

choices.text: Blocking real customers in silence
choices.why: Right. 200 requests in a bad five minutes, from people who did nothing wrong.

choices.text: Nothing, since the limit is per customer
choices.why: The key is IP, so the forty share one count.

prompt: Match each aggregation key to what it counts by.

pairs.right: An address in a header such as X-Forwarded-For
Up to five keys, such as a header and a cookie

prompt: What does a new rule in front of a live site start as, according to this lesson?

choices.text: Block, to stop attacks at once
choices.why: That tests it on customers.

choices.text: Allow, until the team trusts it
choices.why: Allow terminates and skips the later rules.

choices.text: Count
choices.why: Right. A week of counting says what it would have blocked.

choices.text: CAPTCHA, as a compromise
choices.why: It still affects customers, and costs per attempt.

prompt: The second update-web-acl, with the token from before the first, was refused. Why?

choices.text: A rule cannot be set to Count twice
choices.why: The same change would be accepted with a fresh token.

choices.text: The web ACL changed after the read
choices.why: Right. Read again and reapply.

choices.text: moto allows a single update per web ACL per minute
choices.why: AWS refuses the same way.

choices.text: Tokens expire after one second
choices.why: A token is replaced by a change, not by time.

prompt: A CloudWatch Logs group that receives WAF logs must have a name starting with ____. (prefix, with its final hyphen)
hint: moto does not check it; AWS does.

prompt: Match each field of a WAF log record to what it holds.
hint: Decided, tried, the request, the outcome.

prompt: A web ACL with 4 rules, within 1,500 WCU, inspects 20 million requests in a month. What is the month's WAF cost in USD?
Which of these does moto do with the shop's web ACL? Choose all that apply.
hint: It stores, it does not inspect.

choices.text: Stores the rules and their order
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Refuses a stale lock token
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Associates it with the load balancer
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Blocks requests from the IP set
choices.why: moto inspects no traffic.

choices.text: Reports AWS's real capacity units
choices.why: It reported 3, one per rule.

prompt: The shop's 50 million monthly requests move from the base tier to the 2,000 WCU tier. By how many USD a month does the request line grow?
